qc.label_under_test: Small function words in expository or how-to prose that sit right before a clause's verb or a plural noun phrase: expletive 'there' (there are, there needs to be), 'of' after a quantifier (many of, some of, one of), and 'you' before a modal (so you can); quiet for locative 'there', possessive 'of' (roof of the house) and 'you' as an object

neighbours.label: Expletive 'there' meaning 'there is/are/may be' (e.g. 'because there may be added sugar'), strongest mid-sentence in explanatory prose; quiet for locative 'over there'. Other small words (generic 'you can', 'many of', 'exactly') fire it only weakly
